body.purpose: Explanations, reply content, longer prose. Cap at 65ch. Apply text-wrap: pretty.

title.purpose: Post titles, modal headings, section labels. Ceiling: 1.25rem.

label.purpose: Author names, badge text, button labels, form labels. The workhorse weight.

mono.purpose: ZP balance in the header, tabular numeric display. tabular-nums feature active.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Modals and dropdown menus only. Ambient and diffuse. Not applied to post cards.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: State transitions: hover, focus, active changes.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrance transitions: dropdown open, modal appear.

motion.name: duration-micro
motion.purpose: Button hover, focus ring, icon swap. Below perceptual threshold.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Color transitions, border changes, opacity shifts.

motion.name: duration-enter
motion.purpose: Dropdown/modal entrance. Long enough to orient, short enough to not block.

narrative.overview:
Zigma Points is a live community ledger — every point request is a public proposal, every vote is a statement, and every settled outcome is a fact the group made together. The design serves that dynamic. It's a scoreboard, not a timeline. Outcomes land with clarity. Votes feel consequential. The feed reads fast. When the group is watching, nothing should be ambiguous.

The system is product-register first: design disappears into the task. Users aren't here to scroll — they're here to vote, post, and check the standings. Every surface prioritizes scannability over decoration. Inter runs every label, the semantic color vocabulary carries meaning without ornament, and flat tonal surfaces keep focus on the content, not the chrome.

This system explicitly rejects social-media clone grammar — no algorithmic feed aesthetics, no endless passive scroll, no engagement-bait visual patterns. It also rejects the gamified trophy-case aesthetic — no streaks, no progress rings, no confetti. Points matter because the community says so. The design respects that weight.
keyCharacteristics: High-contrast, fast reads — outcomes scannable in under two seconds
Semantic color vocabulary — chromatic color carries meaning, not decoration
Flat tonal layering — no shadows; depth from surface contrast and borders
Bold and clear affordances — no ambiguity about what's interactive
App-first — mobile touch targets and interaction patterns throughout
Inter + JetBrains Mono — humanist warmth for UI, technical precision for data

rules.name: The Semantic First Rule
rules.body: Chromatic color is reserved for semantic meaning: award outcomes are emerald, deduct/error states are red, pending states are amber. No decorative use of color is permitted until a brand accent is formally added to the token system.

rules.name: The No Chroma Creep Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce new chromatic colors outside the semantic set without a formal token decision. One-off accent colors added directly in components fracture the system.

rules.name: The One-Size Rule
rules.body: No element inside the app shell uses a font size above 1.5rem. There is no hero here. Hierarchy is weight and color, not scale.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift at rest. The sole exception is overlays (modals, dropdown menus, popovers) — these must feel above the page plane, not just different from it.

rules.name: The Vote Clarity Rule
rules.body: When a vote is cast, the active button is full-fill — not a border shift, not a tint change. The difference between 'I voted' and 'voting is open' must be unmistakable at a glance on a 390px screen.

rules.name: The No Nested Cards Rule
rules.body: Never place a Card inside another Card. This pattern does not exist in the current codebase; do not introduce it.

dos: Do use semantic colors to carry outcome meaning — emerald for Award/Agree/Awarded, red for Deduct/Disagree/Error, amber for Pending.
Do keep post card surfaces flat with border-subtle (1px) as the sole depth cue. No card shadows.
Do use Inter 500 (label weight) for all button text, badge text, and interactive labels.
Do make vote buttons full-width and full-fill when active.
Do use text-wrap: pretty on explanation and reply text to prevent orphans.
Do maintain ≥ 44px touch targets on all interactive elements.
Do show skeleton states while the feed loads. Not spinners in the content well.
Do use JetBrains Mono for ZP balance numbers and any tabular numeric display.
Do keep text-muted at oklch(0.556 0 0) or darker. Never lighten secondary text for elegance.
donts: Don't build social media clone patterns — no Twitter/Reddit feed grammar, no trending/explore surfaces. The feed is a ledger.
Don't add gamified visuals — no achievement rings, no streak counters, no XP bars, no confetti.
Don't introduce chromatic color outside the semantic set without a formal brand accent decision.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on any card or list item.
Don't add box-shadow to post cards or feed surfaces at rest. Shadows belong on overlays only.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't write secondary text smaller than text-sm (0.875rem) on mobile.
Don't invent non-standard affordances for standard tasks.
Don't place a Card inside another Card.
